overview: Ouray County Historical Society documentation establishes Ironton’s March 1883 founding, more than 100 buildings constructed in 1883, seasonal mid-1880s population of roughly 200 in winter to nearly 1,000 in summer, and its role as the Red Mountain Mining District’s supply and transportation center.

timeline.text: Ouray County Historical Society documentation establishes Ironton’s March 1883 founding, more than 100 buildings constructed in 1883, seasonal mid-1880s population of roughly 200 in winter to nearly 1,000 in summer, and its role as the Red Mountain Mining District’s supply and transportation center.

Otto Mears’ Silverton Railroad reached the Ironton Valley in 1889; by 1890 the town had a permanent population of about 350, utilities, graded streets, plank walks, school, churches, saloons, and other businesses.

Silver decline reduced population to 71 in 1900 and 26 in 1910; later district activity revived for base metals and was consolidated under Idarado before closure in 1978.

moreHistory: Otto Mears’ Silverton Railroad reached the Ironton Valley in 1889; by 1890 the town had a permanent population of about 350, utilities, graded streets, plank walks, school, churches, saloons, and other businesses.
Silver decline reduced population to 71 in 1900 and 26 in 1910; later district activity revived for base metals and was consolidated under Idarado before closure in 1978.
Ouray County records identify several surviving town houses and formal townsite abandonment action in 1975.

Scan/component safeguard: keep the Ironton residential townsite and vanished northern business district separate from Guston, Red Mountain Town, the Silverton Railroad corridor, Larson Brothers Mine, Idarado workings, and other individual mines.
Exact business inventory and every building footprint remain non-blocking uncertainties.
